Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## A Plan for Every Stage of Life

The Conservative Party presents a comprehensive vision for Britain built on the success of their previous five years in government. After inheriting what they describe as an economy "on the brink" following Labour's tenure, the Conservatives claim to have transformed Britain into one of the fastest-growing major economies in the world, halving the deficit and creating record employment levels.

## Economic Security as the Foundation

The manifesto's central premise is that a strong economy underpins everything else—jobs, homes, schools, hospitals, and pensions all depend on continued fiscal discipline. The Conservatives commit to eliminating the deficit through balanced spending reductions, welfare savings, and tackling tax evasion, while pledging no increases to VAT, National Insurance, or Income Tax. They promise to raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000, ensuring those working 30 hours on minimum wage pay no Income Tax.

## Supporting Families and Workers

The plan addresses citizens at every life stage: free childcare expansion to 30 hours for working parents, three million new apprenticeships, Help to Buy schemes, and 200,000 Starter Homes for first-time buyers under 40. The Right to Buy extends to Housing Association tenants, while the benefit cap reduces to £23,000 to ensure work always pays.

## Protecting Public Services

Despite fiscal constraints, the Conservatives pledge real-terms NHS spending increases of £8 billion by 2020, delivering seven-day GP access and same-day appointments for over-75s. Education reforms continue with academy expansion, free schools, and uncapped university places, while maintaining per-pupil funding.

## Security and Sovereignty

The manifesto takes firm positions on immigration control, promising welfare reforms to reduce EU migration and extending "deport first, appeal later" rules. Crucially, they commit to an in-out EU referendum by 2017, seeking renegotiated membership terms while maintaining the Single Market. The Human Rights Act would be replaced with a British Bill of Rights.

## Pensioners and Inheritance

The triple lock pension guarantee continues, while Inheritance Tax effectively rises to £1 million for married couples through a new main residence allowance. Pension freedoms expand, allowing tax-free inheritance of pension pots.

## Conclusion

The Conservatives present themselves as the only party capable of maintaining economic stability against Labour's alleged threat of "economic chaos." Their message: Britain has recovered through hard work and difficult decisions—now is not the time to change course.
